items.title: 61521_David Albert Francis oral history interview
items.q: they put a nickel on one of Jimmy Luntzford's records

ctx.x: No, not Birmingham; not Doltham or none of those places. It was up north -- Andeston, Alabama, I think it was. But anyway, the promoter -- when we got in town, we got in touch with the promoter right away, and he stood good for us to eat, as we hadn't eaten all that day, see, so we got there that evening.

So I'll never forget this -- we got in there and the promoter made the arrangements for us to eat. So somebody came in there, where everybody was sitting down there with their heads down, they were sad and everything. Well, somebody came in and put -- at that time, it was 5¢ for the jukebox. They put -- there was 12 records on the jukebox then -- this was back in 1935, I think it was. Well, they put a nickel on one of Jimmy Luntzford's records, and I don't remember which one it was. I think it was For Dancers…

Well, anyway, they put this nickel on this record, and the record started playing and we all got up and started to dance, and the lady looked up at us and said, 'Lord, they sure was hungry' -- that was after we ate.
